subject: Invoice filename & embedded PO spec — portal vs email fallback

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Invoice submission: filename vs embedded PO (portal fallback)

Hi Dylan / Marissa,

We are ready to start sending invoices for the Q2 run but wanted to confirm the expected ingestion pattern. Our ERP currently stamps the PO on the PDF body, not the filename. We plan to push via SFTP to your portal, but some legacy partners will email invoices to ap@starlite.com (their systems).

Questions:
- If we submit to the portal, do you require the PO to be in a discrete metadata field, or is PO-in-body acceptable?
- For emailed fallback, does Redwood require the PO in the filename/subject? If yes, what exact format should we use (examples appreciated)?
- Do you accept CSV/XML attachments for bulk invoices, or must each invoice be a PDF?

Attaching a sanitized sample CSV line for reference.

Thanks,
Jenny Park
Accounts Payable Lead
Starlite Systems

Attachment: invoice_sample_q2.csv (CSV)

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Jenny Park <jenny.park@starlite.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Jun 2026 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Invoice submission: filename vs embedded PO (portal fallback)

Hi Jenny — thanks for the clear callout. Short answer: portal preferred uses discrete fields; email fallback has a strict filename & subject convention. Details below.

Portal (recommended):
- Use the portal upload API or SFTP UI so you can populate the PO field explicitly. That prevents OCR errors and is the most reliable for automated matching.
- Accepted file types for portal: PDF for single invoices; CSV or XML allowed for bulk payloads if they follow our minimal schema (see link in next email).

Email fallback (when portal/SFTP not possible):
- Required: include PO in both subject and filename. Example patterns we recommend:
  - Subject: INV | PO:98765 | Starlite Systems
  - Filename: PO98765_STL_inv-20260601.pdf
- If you attach a CSV, the filename should still include PO (e.g., PO98765_invoices.csv) and the CSV must contain a header column named PO_NUMBER.
- PDFs with an embedded PO in the body are OK but run through OCR — adds latency and risk of mismatch.

For partners using EDI/XML, we can accept XML if you adhere to our <Invoice><PONumber> node or map via SFTP manifest. If helpful, I can share a minimal JSON/CSV schema.

Next steps:
1) Please confirm whether you can add PO to the portal field for your SFTP pushes.
2) If you must keep PO in-body, let us know so we can add a temporary manual review step (higher SLAs).

I attached a sample PO PDF we received from one of our customers to show format.

Best,
Dylan
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: PO-98765.pdf (PDF)

Subject: Re: Invoice submission: filename vs embedded PO (portal fallback)

Thanks Dylan — very helpful. A couple of clarifications from our side:

- Our AP can easily put PO into the SFTP metadata for portal uploads; that is our preferred route.
- For legacy vendors who email, we control filename templates centrally but need the exact minimal CSV schema for the bulk path. Below is what our exporter currently emits:

CSV sample row (sanitized):
vendor_id,vendor_name,invoice_number,invoice_date,amount,currency,PO_NUMBER,remit_email
STL-001,Starlite Systems,INV-2026-004,2026-06-01,1450.00,USD,98765,ap@starlite.com

Is that sufficient? Also: do you require a separate "vendor_tax_id" field? Our invoices sometimes omit it.

If portal ingestion will accept the CSV as-is (with PO_NUMBER header), we'll route all bulk files that way and reserve email for single exceptions.

Regards,
Jenny
